title: Test-and-Set: Building a Lock with One Atomic Instruction
topic: Test-and-set lock — a single atomic hardware instruction reads a flag's old value and writes one in the same step; threads that read zero own the lock, threads that read one spin until it is released

beats.narration: Two threads, one shared resource — and only one of them can have it at a time.

elements.content: Manimo bobs in centre-screen
How do two threads agree on whose turn it is?

beats.narration: Test and set is one hardware instruction that does two things at once. It reads the lock's old value and writes one — atomically, so no other thread can slip in between.

elements.content: the instruction

TestAndSet(lock, 1):
  old = *lock
  *lock = 1
  return old
Brace marking the three lines as a single atomic step
the read and the write happen as one — nothing can slip between

beats.narration: Two threads race for the lock. Thread one calls test and set first, gets back zero, and walks in. Thread two calls a moment later, gets back one, and has to wait.

elements.content: Thread 1 panel on the left, amber
Thread 2 panel on the right, rose
Centre lock variable with value 0 turning to 1
Arrow from T1 to lock labelled 'TestAndSet → 0'
Arrow from T2 to lock labelled 'TestAndSet → 1'
T1 state flip: READY → HOLDING
T2 state flip: READY → SPINNING

beats.narration: Thread two keeps trying. Each loop reads one, sees the lock is taken, and spins. When thread one finishes its work and writes zero, the very next call returns zero — and now thread two is the holder.

elements.content: Timeline with axes — top row T1 status, middle row lock value, bottom row T2 status
T1 stays HOLDING for first half then RELEASES
Lock value steps: 1 → 1 → 0 → 1 (T2 acquires)
T2 spins (pulsing arc), then becomes HOLDING
Playhead sweeping left to right driven by sprite localTime
spin while busy — the moment the flag drops, the next test-and-set wins

beats.narration: Spin while busy. One atomic step does the test and the set together — and that is the simplest lock in computing.

elements.content: One atomic step. Test, then set.
(this is the spin lock — the simplest mutex in the book)
